You are the assistant of a personal assistant app. Answer the user's message in English, in plain words.
- Answer only from the knowledge base articles and from the results of the tools in this conversation.
- Cite the article IDs you used in square brackets, for example [help-media-02]. Cite none if you used none.
- Never repeat a contact's address in a reply, even one a tool returned.
- Make a change only by calling a tool, and never say a change was made unless a tool result says so.
- Keep a reply to three sentences or fewer.
- If the articles and the tool results do not answer the question, say so in one sentence and stop.

If a tool can answer the message, call it before you answer. Do not refuse a request a tool can serve.

Today's date (UTC) is 2026-12-08.

Knowledge base articles:

[help-media-02] Playing a playlist
A playlist is a list of songs you have saved. To play one, name it. The assistant starts the first song and continues through the list in order unless shuffle is on. Playlists can be created from the songs you name; the assistant lists the songs before it saves the playlist. A playlist cannot hold a song that is not in your library. Changing a playlist does not change what is already playing. To add a song to a playlist, name both.

[help-media-08] Finding music by genre
Name a genre, such as jazz, folk or classical, and the assistant plays music from that genre in your library. If your library has none of that genre, the assistant says so and offers to play a radio station instead. Genres come from the tags on each song, so a song with no tag is not found by genre. To make a playlist from a genre, name the genre and the number of songs you want, and the assistant lists the songs before saving.

[help-media-05] Following a podcast
Follow a podcast to be told when a new episode is released. Ask the assistant to follow a show by name. Episodes play in the order they were released, or the latest first, as you choose. The assistant can play the latest episode, or a named one. Episodes you have started are remembered, so you can resume them later. Unfollowing a show keeps its episodes you have already listened to, but removes it from future reports of new episodes.

[help-media-01] Playing a song from your library
Name the song and, if it helps, the artist. The assistant looks in your music library first and plays the first song that matches. If more than one song has the name, it lists the artists and asks which one you mean. A song that is not in your library cannot be played, and the assistant says so rather than choosing another. Songs play through the device you chose last, unless you name another. The assistant reports the title and the artist when a song starts.

[help-media-03] Shuffle and repeat
Shuffle plays the songs of a playlist or an album in a random order. Turn it on or off by name. Repeat has three settings: off, repeat the current song, and repeat the whole list. The assistant reports the setting after each change. Shuffle does not change the list itself, and turning it off returns to the list's own order from the song now playing. A repeat setting stays until you change it, even when you start something new.

[help-messages-05] Replying to a message
Ask the assistant to reply to the latest message from someone, or to a message you name by its subject. The reply is written in the same thread, so the person sees it with the earlier messages. Say what the reply should say, or ask the assistant to draft a short reply and read it to you first. A reply is sent only after you confirm it. If the thread has more than one earlier message from that person, the assistant asks which one you mean before it replies.

[help-media-07] Adjusting the volume
Volume is a number from zero to one hundred. Ask for a level, or ask for the volume to go up or down by a step. Each step is about ten percent. The assistant reports the new level after each change. A volume limit set by the device stops the assistant from going higher, and it says so when it reaches the limit. Volume changes apply to the device you are using at the moment, unless you name another.

[help-media-09] Pausing, skipping and going back
Pause stops the current song and keeps its place. Resume starts it again from the same point. Skip moves to the next song in the list, and going back moves to the previous one. Going back once more than a few seconds into a song starts that song again from the beginning. Skip does not work on a radio station, because a station is a live stream. The assistant reports what is playing after each of these commands.
play track one from my david bowie playlist

text: To play track one from your David Bowie playlist, first ensure the playlist exists and contains David Bowie songs. Then, name the playlist and specify "track one" to start playing the first song in order. [help-media-02]
